# Resource UNIX group

Create, delete, or modify local UNIX groups

## Related ONTAP commands

```commandline
* vserver services name-service unix-group create
* vserver services name-service unix-group modify
* vserver services name-service unix-group delete
* vserver services name-service unix-group adduser
* vserver services name-service unix-group deluser
```

## Supported Platforms

* On-prem ONTAP system 9.9 or higher
* Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP

## Example Usage

```terraform
# creating a UNIX group
resource "netapp-ontap_unix_group" "unix_group" {
  cx_profile_name = "hw-cluster"
  name = "unix_group"
  svm_name = "svm1"
  users = ["unix_user1", "unix_user2"]
  id = 99
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cx_profile_name` (String) Connection profile name
- `id` (Number) UNIX group ID of the specified group.
- `name` (String) Specifies the name of the UNIX group.
- `svm_name` (String) The name of the SVM.

### Optional

- `users` (Set of String) Users belonging to the UNIX group.

## Import

This resource supports import, which allows you to import existing UNIX group into the state of this resource.
Import require a unique ID composed of the local UNIX group name, svm name and connection profile, separated by a comma.

id = `name`,`svm_name`,`cx_profile_name`

### Terraform Import

For example

```shell
 terraform import netapp-ontap_unix_group.example test_unix_group,svm1,hw-cluster
```

!> The terraform import CLI command can only import resources into the state. Importing via the CLI does not generate configuration. If you want to generate the accompanying configuration for imported resources, use the import block instead.

### Terraform Import Block

This requires Terraform 1.5 or higher, and will auto create the configuration for you

First create the block

```terraform
import {
  to = netapp-ontap_unix_group.unix_group_import
  id = "test_unix_group,svm1,hw-cluster"
}
```

Next run, this will auto create the configuration for you

```shell
terraform plan -generate-config-out=generated.tf
```

This will generate a file called generated.tf, which will contain the configuration for the imported resource

```terraform
# __generated__ by Terraform
# Please review these resources and move them into your main configuration files.
# __generated__ by Terraform from "test_unix_group,svm1,hw-cluster"
resource "netapp-ontap_unix_group" "unix_group_import" {
  cx_profile_name = "hw-cluster"
  name = "test_unix_group"
  svm_name = "svm1"
}
```
